title: What “Better for You” Means to The Fresh Factory
summary: We’re committed to better-for-you food manufacturing and supporting cleaner label brands. Here’s what that means at The Fresh Factory.
body_markdown:
[Innovation](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog-categories/innovation/) ,


[Manufacturing](https://thefreshfactory.co/blog-categories/manufacturing/)


October 15, 2026


At The Fresh Factory, you’ll hear us talk a lot about better-for-you foods and beverages. In fact, our[corporate vision](https://thefreshfactory.co/company2/) is “to become the premier manufacturer helping provide cleaner-label, plant-based, and better-for-you options for the food and beverage industry.”


But what does “better for you” mean, and why do we care about it so much?


## Defining “Better for You”


At its most basic, you can think of “better for you” as what we’re NOT adding to our products:


- No artificial colors
- No artificial flavors
- No artificial preservatives


But that’s our baseline, not our finish line. Beyond that, better for you looks different for every brand we work with. For some, it’s gluten-free or organic. For others, it’s less sugar, more protein, or more fiber. Our job is to help each brand deliver on its own definition and values, without compromising on the fundamentals.


We also believe[ingredient sourcing](https://thefreshfactory.co/food-logistics/) plays a huge role in creating better-for-you products. People want to know what’s in their food and where it comes from. It’s why 50% of our ingredients are sourced locally.


In 2024, we purchased 5.8M lbs of produce from farmers. Any ingredients we can’t source locally are obtained from a trusted network of farmers and distributors around the country.


## Co-manufacturing with Values


Being in the clean food space isn’t greenwashing for us. When we started on this path a decade ago, we were in the minority. The infrastructure wasn’t in place to bring better-for-you products to market at scale, according to our CEO and Co-founder Bill Besenhofer.


“The old players didn’t want to handle some of the unique ingredients and requirements for cleaner foods, because it’s not your prototypical manufacturing structure,” he adds.


The reality is that **cleaner products are harder to make** . Artificial ingredients exist for a reason. Synthetic colors stay bright. Artificial preservatives keep products stable on the shelf for months. Take them out, and manufacturing gets a lot more complicated.


Natural colors from fruits, vegetables, and spices can fade or shift with heat and light. Fresh produce varies from season to season and harvest to harvest, so flavor, color, and texture need constant attention to stay consistent. And without artificial preservatives, food safety and shelf life depend on getting the process exactly right.


Many legacy manufacturers are built for long runs of the same shelf-stable formulas. Better-for-you brands need something different.


At The Fresh Factory, we’ve built our operation around those challenges:


- **Flexible processing:** We have expertise in formulating products that require hot-fill, cold-fill, and high-pressure processing (HPP), so each product gets the method that best protects its taste, nutrition, and safety.
- **Certifications and controls:** We hold a number of[certifications](https://thefreshfactory.co/certifications/) , including Safe Quality Food, gluten-free, non GMO, OU-Kosher, and organic. Our ingredient traceability and testing protocols help brands back up the claims on their labels.
- **In-house food science:** Our[R&D](https://thefreshfactory.co/food-development/) team helps brands reformulate products to remove artificial ingredients without sacrificing the flavor and texture their customers love.


##
Your Better-for-You Partner


A decade ago, we bet that consumers would demand cleaner, more transparent food, and that the brands answering that call would need a manufacturing partner who believed in it as much as they did. Today, we’re proud to be that partner.


Better for you is a promise to the brands we work with and their end customers. But most importantly, it’s a commitment we choose every day.


“We have actually turned away bigger customers who use artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives and aren’t willing to clean up their products,” says Donna Duwe, Executive Vice President of Sales at The Fresh Factory. “As a salesperson, it’s hard giving up business. But we really subscribe to the philosophy, ‘food is medicine.’ We’ve devoted ourselves to customers who believe in that vision.”
